# Salvage
Salvage is both an effective source of income for new players and a critical keystone of your faction's industrial facilities. While some parts for construction have to be bought, and others manufactured via factory lines or microforges, advanced components, the manufacturing schematics of which has been lost both to time and NanoTrasen DRM mechanisms, have to be salvaged from pre-Collapse wrecks to either be sold or used in crafting.
## Techmining
Techmining is effectively the same thing as salvaging for scrap or broken machinery; except instead of searching for scrap, profiteers raid derelicts and wrecks in space for technological artifacts left behind in one of the many skirmishes either post or pre-Collapse.
The most common of these are [color=#ebb72a]survey data disks[/color], while uncommon salvage like Limited Production Chips ([color=#ebb72a]LPC[/color]s), [color=#ebb72a]fabdisks[/color] come second. These are used to boost the research capacity of a research facility, print ships at a shipyard, and unlock specific blueprints when used on a research server, respectively.
## The Abyssal Scrapsea
The [color=#9c1a00]Abyssal Scrapsea[/color] is a sub-area of the [color=#9c1a00]Taypani Abyss[/color] only accessible using specialized FTL disks purchased from [color=#ebb72a]wandering traders[/color], the [color=#ebb72a]Imperial Scribe Outpost[/color], or found in the wild in the [color=#ebb72a]Deepwilds[/color] or [color=#ebb72a]Hadal Deadspace[/color].
Loot found in the [color=#9c1a00]Abyssal Scrapsea[/color] is extremely valuable, ranging from precursor ship weaponry, survey data, corporate databases, bluespace parts, and even blueprints for NanoTrasen and AI ships themselves. As a result, they tend to be extremely high-risk zones, packed to the brim with hostile NPC's, automated defense turrets, and traps, as well as the risk of other players encroaching on your salvage run.
